description: Non-blind development cases derived from the Q3 external diagnostic miss families. These cases may be used for scorer development; Q3 must be treated as spent diagnostic evidence after this file is used.
selection_policy: Exact misses and near-neighbor guard cases covering polymer miscibility/adhesion, ceramic nitride-oxide mismatch, Fe-base steel joining, and same-family III-V buffered heterostructures.

pairs.citation: ACS Omega 2020, PA6/ABS-compatibilized blends via in situ reactive extrusion
pairs.evidence_basis: PA6/ABS requires reactive compatibilization to overcome immiscibility and poor interfacial adhesion.

pairs.citation: Polymer blend compatibility handbook notes on nylon/ABS compatibilized blends
pairs.evidence_basis: Nylon/ABS blends generally need compatibilizer chemistry to suppress phase separation and weak adhesion.

pairs.citation: PolymerDatabase.com, polymer blend compatibility and polarity mismatch notes
pairs.evidence_basis: PVC and PA6 have polarity, hydrogen-bonding, and processing-window mismatch without tailored compatibilizer chemistry.

pairs.citation: Fluoropolymer surface treatment and adhesive bonding technical literature
pairs.manual_source: Ebnesajjad, Fluoroplastics, Volume 2: Melt Processible Fluoropolymers, William Andrew
pairs.evidence_basis: Untreated PTFE has very low surface energy and is a poor direct adhesive substrate for epoxy bonding.

pairs.citation: MatWeb and commercial wear-grade PPS/PTFE filled compound technical data
pairs.evidence_basis: PTFE-filled high-temperature thermoplastic compounds are used as low-friction PPS-type wear grades.

pairs.citation: Kingery, Bowen, and Uhlmann, Introduction to Ceramics, 2nd edition
pairs.evidence_basis: Hexagonal boron nitride and silica have dissimilar chemistry, thermal behavior, and bonding requirements for direct dense ceramic integration.

pairs.citation: Kingery, Bowen, and Uhlmann, Introduction to Ceramics, 2nd edition
pairs.evidence_basis: BN and silica-network glasses lack a simple direct sintering/bonding mechanism without engineered interlayers.

pairs.citation: ASM Handbook Vol. 6, Welding, Brazing, and Soldering; stainless/carbon steel joining guidance
pairs.manual_source: ASM Handbook Vol. 6, Welding, Brazing, and Soldering, ASM International
pairs.evidence_basis: Austenitic stainless and carbon steel can be mechanically joined or welded with appropriate filler and corrosion design controls in non-corrosive service.

pairs.citation: ASM Handbook Vol. 6, Welding, Brazing, and Soldering; stainless/low-alloy steel joining guidance
pairs.manual_source: ASM Handbook Vol. 6, Welding, Brazing, and Soldering, ASM International
pairs.evidence_basis: Fe-base stainless and low-alloy steels are joinable with appropriate filler and service corrosion controls.

pairs.citation: ASM Handbook Vol. 13B, Corrosion: Materials, dissimilar-metal galvanic compatibility guidance
pairs.manual_source: ASM Handbook Vol. 13B, Corrosion: Materials, ASM International
pairs.evidence_basis: High-strength aluminum alloys coupled to passive stainless steel are galvanically risky in conductive wet environments.

pairs.citation: Adachi, Properties of Semiconductor Alloys: Group-IV, III-V and II-VI Semiconductors, 2009
pairs.evidence_basis: InAs/InP is a same-family III-V heterostructure pairing used in optoelectronic and quantum-device contexts with strain or buffer management.

pairs.citation: Adachi, Properties of Semiconductor Alloys: Group-IV, III-V and II-VI Semiconductors, 2009
pairs.evidence_basis: Same III-V family membership is not enough when lattice mismatch and growth penalties are extreme.
